prompt: 'So you're saying the deadline feels impossible with the current team?'
why: Repeating the gist in your own words is reflecting back.
trap: A summary comes at the end; this mirrors one point now.

prompt: 'If I've got it right, you'd rather work mornings?'
why: Checking you heard correctly by restating is reflecting back.
trap: It isn't asking what a word means; it restates.

prompt: When she restated his point, he corrected one detail she'd misunderstood.
The support agent repeats the problem back before trying to fix it.
why: Restating first shows the customer they were heard.
trap: It delays the fix, but the move is restating.

prompt: Repeating word for word felt robotic, so he started using his own words.
why: Good reflecting uses your own words.
trap: It isn't a summary; it's mirroring one point.

prompt: 'You're upset because your tower fell down,' the parent says.
why: Restating what happened shows you heard.
trap: It names a feeling too, but the clue is restating the event.
